audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in the entry says Stand United can be interrupted, and spikes[1] instead states flatly that 'Shen's R lets him abandon the lane with no penalty'.
audit.why: Stand United is a channel and any hard CC cancels it. Tahm Kench is one of the few top laners who can deny it from lane range: the 3-stack Tongue Lash stun or the Abyssal Dive knockup both cancel the channel outright, at 900 and 1000-1200 units respectively, on a 200-second ultimate at rank 1. Cancelling one Shen ult is worth more than every trade in the lane combined, and the entry tells the reader the opposite — that his R is free.
audit.corrected: Bank three An Acquired Taste stacks before you shove, so that when he channels Stand United the stun is ready. Cancelling it costs him 200 seconds and a teamfight.
sources: champ-data/_kits/shen.json (R Stand United, flags.channel 'interruptible — any CC cancels it')

audit.whatIsWrong: _missing-interactions.json phrases the same interaction as 'Shen's Stand United (R) is a channel — your Tongue Lash (Q) cancels it outright.'
audit.why: Tongue Lash only cancels a channel when it stuns, which requires three An Acquired Taste stacks already on Shen. With zero to two stacks it applies a slow, and a slow does not interrupt a channel. Applying that row as written would tell every Tahm Kench player that any Q denies Shen's ultimate, which fails at the exact moment it matters and hands the enemy team a free flank.
audit.corrected: The 3-stack Tongue Lash stun cancels Stand United. A bare Tongue Lash slow does not. Abyssal Dive's knockup also cancels it and does not care about stacks.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Q Tongue Lash: stun only at 3 stacks; W Abyssal Dive knockup)

audit.whatIsWrong: Shen's energy economy is never mentioned anywhere.
audit.why: Shen is an energy champion with a 200-point pool. Twilight Assault costs 140 energy at rank 1 and Shadow Dash costs 150. He physically cannot cast both in one trade early, and after either one he is close to empty. That is the whole shape of the early lane against a champion whose only pressure is the taunt: if he has just Q'd the wave, the taunt is not coming, regardless of what its cooldown says. It is a far better tell than any cooldown timer and it is absent from both layers.
audit.corrected: Watch his energy bar, not just the Shadow Dash timer — Q is 140 and E is 150 out of 200, so he only ever has one of them available.
sources: champ-data/_kits/shen.json (resource Energy, Q cost 140/130/120/110/100, E cost 150)

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit's Refuge is described as blocking trades generally: 'his W sword blocks an auto you need to complete the 3-stack window', 'Ki Barrier and W auto-block eat your 3-stack window', 'Do not chase him into the sword'.
audit.why: Spirit's Refuge blocks basic attacks only. Tongue Lash is a spell and passes through it untouched, applying its damage, its slow and its An Acquired Taste stack. So the refuge does not stall your stacking, it only halves the rate — and the correct play is to keep stacking with Q from outside it rather than backing off entirely, which is what the entry currently teaches.
audit.corrected: Spirit's Refuge eats autos, never Tongue Lash. Keep stacking with Q through the block instead of disengaging.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twilight Assault's max-health scaling is never mentioned, while the entry's build plan is Heartsteel.
audit.why: Twilight Assault deals damage based on the target's max health, and is greatly empowered when the blade collides with a champion. Stacking Heartsteel against Shen scales up the ability he uses to farm and to trade. Worth knowing before the item is bought, not after.
audit.corrected: Twilight Assault reads your max health — Heartsteel stacks make his Q hit you harder, so take resistances alongside it.

audit.whatIsWrong: late says 'Your Abyssal Voyage mirrors his global impact; coordinate with your team on timing so your R and his R are not both active at once'.
audit.why: Tahm Kench has no global ultimate. The live W is Abyssal Dive, a 1000-1200 range knockup on 21/20/19/18/17, and the R is Devour, a single-target removal. There is nothing to coordinate against Stand United's 35000 range, and a player told he has a global equivalent will make rotation calls he cannot back up.
audit.corrected: You have no global. What you have is the ability to cancel his — hold three stacks when you expect the channel.

edits.after: Stand United is a channel and hard CC cancels it — hold three stacks when you shove so the Tongue Lash stun, or an Abyssal Dive knockup, denies the 200s ultimate.

edits.before: Shen's 4-5 is where this lane tilts his way hardest: his E taunt is up frequently, his Ki Barrier refills every trade, and his W sword blocks an auto you need to complete the 3-stack window. You have no ultimate escape and he can freely reset the lane tempo. Do not chase him into the sword, and never all-in without 3 stacks banked — without the stun, Devour is just a brief removal that he walks away from at full Ki Barrier. Farm efficiently and activate your E to convert grey health into shield during any extended trade. At 6 his R immediately gives him a global safety valve; the moment you shove the wave expect him to abandon lane and deny you any tower damage.
edits.after: Shen's 4-5 is where this lane tilts his way hardest: his taunt is up often and Ki Barrier refills every trade. But Spirit's Refuge only blocks basic attacks — Tongue Lash is a spell and passes straight through, stack and all, so keep stacking with Q from outside the sword instead of disengaging. Never all-in without 3 stacks banked; without the stun, Devour is a brief removal he walks out of. Farm efficiently and press E to convert grey health mid-trade rather than banking it. Twilight Assault reads your max health, so pair the Heartsteel with resistances instead of more HP. At 6 his R is a channel, not a free exit: shove with three stacks in hand and the moment he starts it, stun him out of it.

edits.before: By 2+ items both of you are near-unkillable frontliners and the lane result largely equalizes into teamfight contribution — your Devour removes a carry from a fight, his R saves a carry across the map, and neither kit hard wins the pure tank mirror. Play for the Devour on their most valuable non-tank, not on Shen himself. Your Abyssal Voyage mirrors his global impact; coordinate with your team on timing so your R and his R are not both active at once, and look to catch him pre-6 windows in the side lane where his global is down.

notes: Two things worth escalating beyond this matchup. First, the _missing-interactions.json row for tahmkench/shen says 'your Tongue Lash (Q) cancels it outright' — that is only true at three An Acquired Taste stacks, since Tongue Lash is a slow until then and slows do not break channels. Any owner applying that row verbatim will publish advice that fails in the exact moment it is needed. Second, Shen's energy costs (140 for Q, 150 for E, out of a 200 pool) are the strongest laning tell in the matchup and appear nowhere in either layer; the generator appears to reason purely from cooldowns and never from resource costs, which will be understating every energy champion across the site.
